newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's LPMO buys 7,693 tonnes of frozen beef.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's LPMO buys 7,693 tonnes of frozen beef.

text.p: South Korea's state-run Livestock Products Marketing Organisation (LPMO) said on Tuesday it bought a total of 7,693 tonnes of frozen beef through tenders last Tuesday and Thursday.
An official with the organisation said it bought 2,483 tonnes of U.S. beef, 162 tonnes of Canadian beef, 4,838 tonnes of Australian beef and 210 tonnes of New Zealand beef.
The official said the organisation had invited tenders for 8,428 tonnes, but passed on 735 tonnes due to high prices.
U.S. and Canadian chuck roll was bought at an average of $3,199 per tonne on a cost and freight basis, traders said.

Australian and New Zealand grain-fed bone-in beef was bought at an average of $2,128 a tonne, grass-fed fullset was bought at an average of $2,631 and grass-fed bone-in beef at an average of $1,738, they said.
Arrivals were set for Seoul (5,576 tonnes), Pusan (775 tonnes), Taegu (380 tonnes) and Naju (962 tonnes).
Shipment of 3,621 tonnes was slated for August 20 and 4,072 tonnes for August 31.
